title: eps-ground-rupture — interactive companion to Chiama et al. (2025)
description:
A reproducible data-processing pipeline and companion website for the two-dimensional distinct element method (DEM) surface-rupture analyses of Chiama et al. (2025). The website brings together five interactive Tableau Public dashboards and the Ground Rupture Explorer. The pipeline cleans and organizes published simulation outputs and field measurements into Parquet tables, defines analytical views in DuckDB, checks results with automated tests, and exports the data used by the dashboards and explorer. The site explains the analyses and documents differences from the paper's published figures.

The Ground Rupture Explorer lets readers choose modeled geological conditions and a range of fault slip (movement), then examine the corresponding results from existing simulations. It shows distributions and summary statistics for scarp height, deformation zone width, and scarp dip. Readers can download a ZIP containing the matching simulation records and summary statistics as CSV files, the scenario settings, a record of data sources and versions, and a Microsoft Word report containing the scenario, statistics, and charts. Each chart can also be saved as an image. This research tool helps readers investigate simulated ground rupture. It does not predict what will happen at a particular site.

This record identifies the software and website. It does not replace the citation for the paper, nor for the underlying data, which is deposited separately on DesignSafe-CI. The explorer's data files are not part of this archive: they are published as release assets of the GitHub repository. Those built from the DEM experiments are distributed under the Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By 1.0), and the field-data file under CC BY 4.0, each with attribution to its sources.

Figures. This archive contains none of the paper's figures: they remain © The Author(s) 2025 under the publisher's author-sharing terms — non-commercial use, no derivatives — which are not this record's Apache-2.0 licence, so the repository excludes them from release archives (git export-ignore). The companion website shows four of them, reproduced from the authors' accepted manuscript with the full citation alongside; only Figures 1 and 2 are withheld there, because they embed photographs belonging to other authors.

Photographs. The archive includes two photographs shown with the explorer's sample scenarios, each under its own terms and not this record's Apache-2.0 licence: Liu Shu fu / Office of the President, Taiwan, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0; and D. H. Kupfer, U.S. Geological Survey, 1952, U.S. public domain.
